gold.summary: Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.

candidates.title: Process-group cleanup still leaves detached descendants alive
candidates.detail: The new cleanup only signals and checks the original process group. Descendants that create another session or process group survive invocation completion. This existing limitation leaves the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-nUbs7Q/claude-501/review-377/detached.ts`. The fixture launches a Python child with start_new_session=True and redirected stdio. Output: `Invocation exit: 0 ; detached child alive after return: true`, followed by `AssertionError: background descendant must not outlive invocation`. The fixture killed its surviving child afterward.
candidates.failure_scenario: An implementer's tool launches a detached background writer. The agent exits or is stopped, but the writer survives and continues changing worktree files during cleanup.

gold.summary: Run-wide scratch roots let one invocation cleanup kill another invocation writer.

candidates.title: Working-directory matching kills unrelated orphan processes
candidates.detail: A recent birth time, orphan status, and matching cwd do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated processes and sends them termination signals. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-p4xl5T/claude-501/review-unrelated-process.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: unrelated orphan started by the caller must survive another invocation` followed by `false !== true`.
candidates.failure_scenario: Two activities share a working directory. While one invocation runs, the other starts an orphaned platform process with a hidden environment. The first invocation finishes and kills the second activity's process solely because its cwd and birth time match.

gold.summary: The owner_diagnostics foreign keys cascade on delete without an index on event_id or invocation_id, so the daemon's synchronous debug-event cleanup scans the whole table for every deleted event and slows as owner rows grow.

Running `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"probe":"rollback database boundary","raw":{"text":"RAW_OWNER_HOLDOUT_MARKER"},"allowsDefault":true,"hasReadDenial":false}`. Real Seatbelt execution was unavailable inside this sandbox; the persisted row and base profile were checked directly.
candidates.failure_scenario: The new release records verifier diagnostics, deployment rolls back to the base release, and an implementing agent reads owner_diagnostics directly from the database using its permitted filesystem access.
